Offene Vokale + Öffnungsdiphthonge. NEU: nyai (Thunyaiphat: ny+ai Trigraph), yao (Thai เยา [jaːo]: Yaowapha), aue (Auemporn: au+e Vokalgruppe), aew (Thai [kɛːw]: Kaew-Namen), uang (Thai [uaŋ]: Duang, Puang, Kuang – 21 Namen!), ae (Thai [ɛː]: Maemae, Taevivat, Saenkham), oua (Lao: Moua), ia (Thai/Lao [ia]: Thiani, Somphian, Wichian), ew (Digraph als aew-Coda), ua (Thai [ua]: Chua, Tuah, Maruai), uai (Lao [uaj]: Maruai), ear (Thearnthong: Thai-ae mit r-Schreibung). Reihenfolge: längste zuerst.

Halboffene Vokale. NEU: euang (Thai/Lao เอือ [ɯːaŋ]: Sibounheuang), yoen (Kongyoen: Thai [joːn]), yoo (Thai ยู: Yooyen), oeng (Thai เอิ/เอือ: Rungrueng, Chanrueng), oen (Thai -เอิน: Lasungnoen, Tedsungnoen), ueng (Thai เอือง [ɯːaŋ]: Nuengmajcha), eun (Lao -eun: Chaleunsouk), oe (Thai เ-า Langvokal: Koedchatturat, Sipaseuth), eu (Thai เ- [ɯː]: Preuksapanich), eo (Thai/Lao [ɛːo]: Keo, Charoen-Namen), iong (Lao: Xiong), yaa (Thai/Lao langer aa-Vokal: Juaa, Punyaa, Chaiyaanunt), io (Thai [io]: Siorat), ue (Thai/Lao [ɯː]: Vue, Lue, Chuena). Reihenfolge: Tetragraph vor Trigraph vor Digraph zwingend.
Geschlossene Vokale. NEU: iu (Thai [iːu] einsilbig: Thiu).
